newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed, investors await Telekom.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed, investors await Telekom.

text.p: European stock markets opened mixed on Monday with the major investor focus fixed firmly on the 20 billion mark ($13.28 billion) flotation of Germany's Deutsche Telekom.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar was trading below its overnight peaks after Japan recorded the first increase in its trade surplus with the United States in 20 months.
German shares fell in early bourse trade, with dealers saying that the market was on hold ahead of the debut during the morning of Telekom, Europe's biggest telecommunications company.
"There's only one subject to today and that's Telekom. Don't go looking for much action elsewhere in the market," said one Frankfurt trader.
Deutsche Telekom shares were expected to rise above their 28.50 mark issue price as institutional investors, disappointed by their allocation, try to buy more shares on the open market.
The shares were quoted at between 32.50 and 33 marks in the pre-debut grey market, but one trader said he expected early trading levels to be erratic.
"Some of the foreign allotments were very disappointing. The UK portion was very, very small," one trader said.

Shares will trade on all eight of Germany's regional stock exchanges with the first price quotes expected by mid-morning. They will be listed on the New York Stock Exchange later in the day and will make their debut in Tokyo on Tuesday.

With annual sales of 66 billion marks, Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecommunications group and one of Germany's biggest corporations. Its listing will be second in size only to the huge offering of Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
London shares opened firm but slid into negative ground in early trade, while French equities fell more than 0.6 percent as investors took profits following the bourse's year-high on Friday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 14.12 points at 2,226.21 at 1015 GMT.
Via Banque was 3.34 percent up at 164 francs on expectations Banque Paribas will sell the unit but was off its early highs.

Paribas itself fell 1.38 percent to 363 francs after a 12 percent rally last week. Carmaker Renault, which rose on Friday despite weak sales figures and a profit warning, joined the downward trend and dropped 1.79 percent to 120.9 francs.
London's FTSE 100 index of leading British shares opened slightly firmer on hopes of a fresh wave of takeovers.
But the market swiftly erased early gains, led lower by declining equity futures and British government bonds, or gilts.
The gilts market earlier rose on news that Britain had repaid a larger than expected 4.4 billion pounds ($7.33 billion) of public sector debt in October.

Shares in British Gas were the main focus, climbing 13 pence to 222 by 1030 GMT following press reports that Royal Dutch/Shell had approached the gas utility with plans for a 40 billion pound merger. Both firms have declined to comment.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar was below its peaks against the mark and near overnight highs against the yen in early European trade.

Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus for October fell 12.9 percent from a year ago, but its trade surplus with the U.S. surged in October for the first time in 20 months as Japanese car makers took advantage of a weaker yen.
"The headline data was disappointing, but the bilateral surplus was positive. They pretty much cancelled each other out," said Paul Meggyesi, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
By 1015 GMT the dollar was quoted at 111.28 yen and 1.5053 marks, compared with 111.12 yen and 1.5076 marks in late European trade on Friday.

"Any relief from dollar/yen was quickly curtailed by the fact that the bilateral surplus with the U.S. increased for the first time in 20 months, driven by a pretty impressive rise in car exports," said Meggyesi.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.28 yen and 1.5053 marks, compared with 111.12 yen and 1.5076 marks in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1045 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 2.1 points at 3,956.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 14.2 points at 2,226.13.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 15.55 points at 2,780.25.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $379.70 against $379.25 on Friday afternoon and $379.85 in the morning. Silver firmed seven points to $4.92.
